intro: Learn countries, nationalities, and languages in Spanish. Discover how nationality adjectives form their feminine and agree with nouns.
b1.titulo: From the country to the person
b1.texto:
To talk about origin and nationality, we use the verb **ser** with adjectives or with the preposition **de**:

- Adjectives ending in **-o** change to **-a** in the feminine: *italiano / italiana*, *chino / china*.
- Adjectives ending in a consonant add **-a** and drop the written accent: *francés / francesa*, *alemán / alemana*, *japonés / japonesa*.
- Some adjectives have only one form for masculine and feminine: *estadounidense*, *marroquí*.

Country names always start with a capital letter (*Francia*, *Japón*). In contrast, nationalities and languages are always written with lowercase letters (*francés*, *japonés*).

Many nationality adjectives also name the language itself (*el francés*, *el chino*). Remember that after the verb **hablar**, the definite article is omitted: we say **hablo francés**.
b2.f3.texto: Yes, she speaks Spanish and French.
b4.texto:
Notice the gender agreement with the subject pronoun:

- **Masculine**: Pablo es español.
- **Feminine**: Ana es española.

Notice how adjectives with a final accent on -és or -án drop the written accent when adding the feminine -a (alemán → alemana, francés → francesa).
b5.f0.texto: France is a very large and beautiful country located in Europe.
b5.f1.texto: Marie lives in the capital city together with two good friends.
b5.f2.texto: She always speaks French at the newly opened university campus.
b5.f3.texto: Kenji is Japanese and studies very diligently here in Madrid.
b5.f4.texto: He speaks Japanese very fluently and is learning Spanish daily.
b5.f5.texto: The enthusiastic students learn foreign languages with great joy.
b6.pregunta: Which nationality has the same form for a man and a woman?
b6.o0.refuerzo: Correct: estadounidense ends in -e and works for both men and women.
b6.o1.refuerzo: Incorrect: the feminine form of italiano is italiana.
b6.o2.refuerzo: Incorrect: the feminine form of japonés is japonesa.
b7.pregunta: Complete the sentence with the correct form.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Correct: Marie is female, so we use the feminine form francesa.
b7.o1.refuerzo: Incorrect: francés is the masculine form.
b7.o2.refuerzo: Incorrect: Francia is the name of the country, not the nationality.
b8.frase: Tokio es la capital de Japón.
b8.traduccion: Tokyo is the capital of Japan.
b9.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «I am from Italy».
p.Francia.consejo: European country neighbouring Spain. Written with a capital letter.
p.francés.consejo: Nationality and language. Feminine: francesa (without accent).
p.Alemania.consejo: Central European country. Capitalized in Spanish.
p.alemán.consejo: Nationality and language. Feminine: alemana (without accent).
p.italiano.consejo: Nationality and language. Feminine form: italiana.
p.los Estados Unidos.consejo: Country name that regularly takes a plural masculine article.
p.estadounidense.consejo: Invariable in gender: works for both masculine and feminine.
p.China.consejo: Major Asian country. Written with an initial capital letter.
p.chino.consejo: Nationality and language. Feminine form: china.
p.Japón.consejo: Asian island nation. Written with an accent on the o.
p.japonés.consejo: Nationality and language. Feminine form: japonesa.
p.Marruecos.consejo: North African country, neighbouring Spain to the south.
p.marroquí.consejo: Ends in -í and has identical forms for men and women.
p.el país.consejo: Masculine noun with an accent mark on the i: «el país».
p.la capital.consejo: Feminine noun: «la capital de España es Madrid».
p.el idioma.consejo: Masculine noun despite ending in -a: «el idioma español».
p.francesa.consejo: Feminine of «francés». Adjectives match their noun, so «francesa» fits «mujer» or «lengua». Stress on «THE».
p.ana.consejo: A woman's name that reads the same backwards, «ana». Stress falls on the first syllable: A-na.
p.aprenden.consejo: The «ellos» form of «aprender». The family includes «aprendiz», an apprentice, and «aprendizaje», learning.
p.idiomas.consejo: Plural of «idioma». Looks like English idiom, but this one means a whole language. Stress: i-DYO-mas.
p.gran.consejo: A short form of «grande», used before a noun, both masculine and feminine: «gran alegría», «gran idea».
